Read: Read file from local filesystem. Text returns with line numbers; images shown to you; PDFs as text (`pages` like "1-5" for long ones); notebooks as cells. Absolute path. Large file: read needed part via `offset` (first line, 1-based) + `limit` (line count). Directory = error: use Glob or Bash `ls`.
Write: Create file or replace completely. Overwriting unread file fails. Prefer Edit for partial changes. No documentation files unless asked.
Edit: Replace text in file. `old_string` must match file exactly (indentation included, without Read's line-number prefix) and be unique unless `replace_all` true. Read file first. To create file: empty `old_string`, path not existing yet.
NotebookEdit: Replace, insert or delete one Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) cell. Read notebook first. `cell_id` = cell id or 0-based index. `replace` needs `new_source`; `insert` adds cell after `cell_id` (start if empty), needs `new_source` + `cell_type`; `delete` removes cell. Replaced code cell loses outputs.
Glob: Find files by name pattern (`**/*.rs`, `src/**/test_*.py`). Respects .gitignore. Sorted by modification time, newest first, cut at 100. Open-ended multi-round search: search step by step yourself.
Grep: Search file contents by regex (Rust regex syntax: escape literal braces/parentheses). Respects .gitignore. `output_mode`: `files_with_matches` (default), `content` (matching lines; -n, -A, -B, -C), `count`. Narrow with `glob` ("*.ts") or `type` ("rust"). `multiline` lets pattern span lines. Use instead of grep/rg in Bash.
Bash: Run shell command, return output (stdout+stderr). Working directory persists between calls; other shell state doesn't. For builds, tests, git etc, not reading/searching/editing files: dedicated tools do that better. Quote paths with spaces. Timeout 2 min unless `timeout` set (ms, max 600000). `run_in_background` for servers and slow jobs, then BashOutput + KillShell. No sleep-loops to wait: read output.
BashOutput: Read output a background command (Bash `run_in_background`) produced since last read, and whether it still runs. Optional `filter`: regex, only matching lines return.
KillShell: Stop background command started with Bash `run_in_background`.
TodoWrite: Keep task list for session. Use for work with 3+ steps or several parts. Send whole list every time. Exactly one task `in_progress`; mark `completed` as soon as done, never while tests fail or work partial. Each task: imperative `content` ("Run the tests") + present-continuous `activeForm` ("Running the tests").
ExitPlanMode: In plan mode: present plan, ask user to approve. Call when plan ready, only for tasks writing code, not research. User answers in app; don't ask approval any other way. After approval: leave plan mode, may change files.
AskUserQuestion: Ask user multiple-choice question when blocked on decision only they can make (approach, name, scope). Not for things you can find out yourself or plan approval. Two to four options; recommended first, say so in label. User can always skip or answer in chat.
WebFetch: Fetch URL, keep what matters: page's main content as Markdown, no navigation, banners, sidebars, footers, scripts, styles. With `prompt`: small model answers it from page, you get answer (quote one or two sentences max). Without: cleaned page itself, ~40,000 chars max. Fails for login-gated pages and localhost. HTTP upgraded to HTTPS. Redirect to other host: new URL returned, call WebFetch again with it.
WebSearch: Search web (Brave Search) for current info past training data: recent events, new library versions, docs. Returns titles, URLs, snippets; WebFetch reads a page. Include current year in queries about recent things. After answering from results, end with "Sources:" list of Markdown links. `allowed_domains` limits results to those sites, `blocked_domains` removes them (no wildcards).
Task: Start subagent for self-contained job. Types: `explore` (read-only: Read, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch) for finding things across files / answering code questions; `general-purpose` for multi-step job needing shell or edits; `fork` to branch off this conversation (all said so far as context) for one directive. Others start with no memory of conversation: give whole task (goal, where to look, what to report). Several `explore` in one message search in parallel. `run_in_background`: carry on while it works; report arrives later as task notification, don't wait or poll. `name` allows SendMessage follow-ups. `isolation: "worktree"`: own git worktree, edits don't touch this checkout. Subagent can't ask user or start subagents. Not for lookups doable with one Grep or Read.
SendMessage: Message a subagent you started, by id or name. Running background subagent reads it before next step. Finished one continues with whole history + message as next instruction; new report returns. `run_in_background` continues finished one without waiting.
TaskStop: Stop background subagent still running, by id or name.
